newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM says she unafraid of death threats.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM says she unafraid of death threats.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has said she is not afraid of threats to her life.
"I am not afraid of death or killing. I have faced death warnings several times," she told Parliament on Tuesday night during a stormy debate over law and order.
The prime minister did not specify any death threats. In recent weeks, leaders of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) publicly said "Hasina will not be able to survive."
Hasina spoke after some MPs walked out of Parliament to protest what they said was the government's failure to condemn an attack on a former minister and BNP member.
Former planning minister Moyeen Khan said he was attacked on Tuesday while driving to Dhaka from his hometown of Narsingdi. He said his car was damaged but he was not injured.
Khan who present was in Parliament on Tuesday night, said he thought the attackers were activists of the ruling Awami League.
Home Minister Rafiqul Islam told Parliament he would order an immediate probe.
Former prime minister and BNP head Begum Khaleda Zia led the complaints that the government had taken the attack lightly.

"The Home Minister is taking the attack on our friend very lightly...and the prime minister has failed to issue a statement on this. So it's time we walk out in protest," BNP's deputy leader Badruddoza Chowdhury said before marching out.
Hasina took the floor immediately and said she could not understand what warranted an opposition walkout. She said the BNP not only wanted to "kill me" but also to destroy parliamentary democracy.
